newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power mostly down as demand ebbs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power mostly down as demand ebbs.

text.p: Spot power prices in the western U.S. were mostly lower Thursday amid decreasing demand in the Northwest as well as extra hydropower supplies, market sources said.
"Loads are coming down. Some utilities were selling today that had been buying," said one northern California trader.
Lower prices and larger hydropower sales volumes from the Bonneville Power Administration for Friday schedulings also put downward pressure on spot prices, sources said.

Next-day firm, on-peak power at the California-Oregon border (COB) was last quoted $29.50-30.50 per megawatt hour (MWh), down from $31.00-33.00 on Tuesday. Off-peak COB was quoted $17.50-18.50, down from $18.00-19.00.
Next-day firm, on-peak power at Mid-Columbia was last quoted $31.00-32.00, while off-peak was quoted $18.00-20.00.
Palo Verde next-day firm, on-peak power was quoted $26.00-28.00 per MWh, little changed from Wednesday. Off-peak Palo Verde was quoted $14.00-15.00.
Four Corners firm, on-peak power was also little changed at $25.00-27.00, while off-peak was slightly higher at $15.00-17.00.
